shots.name: the whole page
shots.line: My daughter draws these little comic pages. This one is about me.

shots.name: daddy
shots.line: She told me once that when you dream about flying, it means your soul has nothing to do.

shots.name: the pointing
shots.line: I said, so it's a freeloader. Lives in my house, eats my food, no job.

shots.name: a freeloader
shots.line: She went and wrote the whole thing down.

shots.name: the bunk room
shots.line: What I told her was, when I was a boy I slept on the top bunk. Some nights I came up off the mattress.

shots.name: almost to the ceiling
shots.line: Not far. Close enough to the ceiling that I could see the paint on it.

shots.name: the moon
shots.line: The whole house asleep, the window right there, and the moon.

shots.name: the boy on the wall
shots.line: I never said anything about it at the time. You don't, when you're eight.

shots.name: Dave did too
shots.line: Then Dave tells me he did it too.

shots.name: Dave
shots.line: That's Dave. He works for me. Twenty-two years now.

shots.name: Dave's eyes
shots.line: One afternoon he says it like he's telling me the weather. He used to float.

shots.name: same birthday
shots.line: And he's got my birthday. Same day, same year.

shots.name: back out
shots.line: So there's two of us in one building. I don't know what it means. I know it happened.
